gloss: all show and no substance; failing to live up to one's reputation

definitions.gloss: all show and no substance; failing to live up to one's sign
definitions.explanation: Describes a situation where the outward appearance, reputation, or advertising does not match the actual quality or reality. Literally means the signboard has fallen over — the impressive facade has collapsed.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{看板倒|かんばんだお}れだ。
examples.english: That shop is all show and no substance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧⟦シェフ→シェフ：05062_shefu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{看板倒|かんばんだお}れだった。
examples.english: It was a famous chef's restaurant, but the taste didn't live up to the name.

examples.japanese: ⟦スローガン→スローガン：11629_suroogan⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧で⟦{実行|じっこう}→実行：03274_jikkou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{伴|ともな}わない→伴う：10389_tomonau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{看板倒|かんばんだお}れ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}わざる→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{得|え}ない→得る：02014_eru⟧。
examples.english: Having impressive slogans without follow-through can only be called all talk and no action.

notes:
Literally "the signboard has fallen over" — the impressive sign (⟦{看板|かんばん}→看板：00166_kanban⟧) collapses ({倒|たお}れ), meaning the outward appearance or reputation does not hold up. A vivid metaphor for businesses, policies, or people that promise much but deliver little.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {看板倒|かんばんだお}れ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{終|お}わる: to end up as empty promises
- {看板倒|かんばんだお}れ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{政策|せいさく}→政策：10070_seisaku⟧: a policy that's all talk
- {看板倒|かんばんだお}れ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: so as not to be all show

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名前負|なまえま}け: losing to one's name — when someone or something can't live up to a grand name
- ⟦{有名無実|ゆうめいむじつ}→有名無実：06459_yuumeimujitsu⟧: famous in name only — formal expression for something that exists in name but has no substance
- {羊頭狗肉|ようとうくにく}: sheep's head, dog meat — advertising something fine but selling something inferior (more literary)
